vue.says: svg aria-hidden: the wordmark names it

clusters.title: Base path: the demo reaches the API-mismatch variant, the kit the page-path one

match.detail: (This page was served for the base path|Base path reported by the API)

spec.says: page-path failures are checked before any request; the user sees base path mismatch with page path, server base path and, when it differs, the API's

kit.says: page at /speed/, server configured for /

vue.says: /info reports /speed for a page at / (the API-mismatch variant)

evidence.notes: Opening the Vue demo at /speed/ triggers pageMismatch before any request: the kit's variant.

decision.rationale: The kit shows the page-path variant (page at /speed/, server at /); the demo must reach the same variant to compare its copy. Once it does, what is left is the copy of that variant, a content difference for its own cluster.

actions.what: web/parity/drivers.ts: the Vue side reaches test/basepath by opening the demo at /speed/, so the page-path check fails before any request.

clusters.title: Result status time of day: kit's literal 24-hour sample vs Intl in the active locale

clusters.title: Insufficient-data link: the demo's client is 10.8.0.6, the kit's 192.168.1.42

match.detail: 192\.168\.1\.42.*10\.8\.0\.6|^text "Client IP 192\.168\.1\.42 IPv4 Protocol HTTP/2 Streams # auto Standard preset · Auto streams · No data cap"$|10\.8\.0\.6 IPv4 Protocol h2 Streams — auto, up to 6 Standard preset

spec.says: the 20 kbit/s and 19 kbit/s link of the insufficient-data state; silent on its client address

kit.says: Client IP slow ? '10.8.0.6' : '192.168.1.42' (insufficient is not slow)

decision.rationale: The kit's insufficient-data state uses the LAN client 192.168.1.42; only its slow states use 10.8.0.6.

actions.what: web/src/demo/fixtures.ts infoFor: the insufficient link reports 192.168.1.42; update the fixtures comment.

clusters.title: Slow scenarios: the kit suggests VPN for the private address 10.8.0.6, the spec and demo LAN

spec.says: both client addresses are private, so the suggested label is LAN for each; suggestedLabel is VPN for cgnat, LAN for private

kit.says: sel = ctxSel || (slow ? 'VPN' : 'LAN'); Client IP slow ? '10.8.0.6' : '192.168.1.42'

evidence.notes: The kit's 10.8.0.6 with VPN contradicts the address-class mapping; the spec records LAN for the demo on purpose.

decision.rationale: The spec wins: wire-protocol §5 maps a private address to LAN and frontend.md §9 records LAN for the demo on purpose. The kit's VPN on 10.8.0.6 contradicts the mapping, so the difference is kept until the export fixes it.

actions.what: design-system-upstream.md: the kit's slow client should use a CGNAT address (e.g. 100.101.4.17) if it suggests VPN, or suggest LAN for 10.8.0.6 (wire-protocol §5).

clusters.title: Page host in the header: the kit's speed.home.lan vs the demo's own origin

spec.says: Server name ... in the persistent header with the page's host

kit.says: host: this.props.host || 'speed.home.lan'

evidence.notes: Both follow the spec; the value is where the page is served from. Normalise each side's own page host in the content capture (web/parity/side.ts, capture.ts).

decision.rationale: Both sides show the page's own host as the spec asks; the value depends only on where each page is served from, so the harness treats each side's own host as equal.

actions.what: Replace each side's own page host (prototype speed.home.lan, Vue the demo origin's host) with one token in the content capture before normalisation; unit test; a bullet with its reason in demo-parity.md § What It Compares.

clusters.title: Fully rounded radius: 9999px vs 3.35544e+07px, and the chip width it sits with

kit.says: --radius-full: 9999px

evidence.notes: Both clamp to min(w,h)/2 and render the same pill; compare the effective radius per side.

decision.rationale: 9999px and Tailwind's calc(infinity*1px) both clamp to half the box's height and draw the same pill.

actions.what: web/parity/compare/style.ts: compare a corner radius as min(r, min(width, height)/2) per side, with the length tolerance; unit test; note it in demo-parity.md.

clusters.title: Border colour of a 1px transparent border compared with a 0-width border

spec.says: says nothing on borders of icon or ghost buttons

kit.says: .btn{border:1px solid transparent}

vue.says: ghost and default variants have no border (0 width, currentColor)

evidence.notes: A transparent 1px border and a 0-width border render the same; web/parity/compare/style.ts applies() compares the colour because the kit's side has width.

decision.rationale: A 1px transparent border and a 0-width border render the same; their colours are not a difference.

actions.what: web/parity/compare/style.ts: skip a border colour when one side's border is transparent and the other side's has no width; unit test; note the skip in demo-parity.md.

clusters.title: Data used, duration and packet loss: a 'Test' term/definition list inside Results (kit) vs three tiles after it (Vue)

match.detail: ^(link "Why\?"|text "Data used(?!.* → "Data used")|text "… Idle latency — Jitter — Test" → |term|definition|text "Packet loss" → "Packet loss Browsers can't see packet loss over TCP")( \(#\d+\))?

spec.says: v0.1 metrics include data used, duration and the packet loss slot; packet loss shows "browsers can't see packet loss over TCP" and a link to why

kit.says: a MetaList titled 'Test' (<dl>: Data used, Duration, Packet loss) inside the Results section; packet loss: Not measured badge + Why? link with the reason as tooltip and in its name

vue.says: three tiles in a div after Results; visible reason + Why?

evidence.notes: The spec lists the reason among the qualifiers shown, so the kit's tooltip-only reason contradicts it.

decision.text: Kit layout, spec reason: data used, duration and packet loss move into the Results section as the kit's 'Test' term/definition card with the Not measured badge and the descriptive Why? name, while the packet-loss reason stays visible as the spec lists it among the qualifiers shown.
decision.rationale: The export decides layout and markup (the spec is silent and counts these among the result metrics); the spec decides the reason is shown, so the kit's tooltip-only reason gets an upstream note.

actions.what: TestPage.vue: the three metrics as one 'Test' <dl> card inside the Results section (full width; three columns from sm); packet loss as a Not measured badge, the visible reason and a Why? link named 'Why packet loss is not measured: …'.
design-system-upstream.md: the packet-loss reason is shown text per screens.md §6, not only a tooltip.
